close_reason: Done in da2e168. Added 'Do not move validation from construction to per-request' section to BearerAuth rustdoc (the rationale covers both BearerAuth and BasicAuth since they share the pattern). Five-reason defense against the 'just validate per-request' refactor.
description:
auth.rs:152-180 (BearerAuth) and 200-230 (BasicAuth) store a pre-computed header_string String, validated via HeaderValue::from_str at construction time. auth_header() returns borrows from the stored String.

A contributor may suggest 'just store the token + username/password fields and call HeaderValue::from_str in auth_header() on each request'. This is the wrong simplification.

Defense:
1. Validation at construction means invalid credentials surface at BearerAuth::new() / BasicAuth::new() return value — the caller fails fast at their auth-setup code. Per-request validation pushes failures to the first JmapClient::call() or fetch_session(), which is far from the bug source and harder to debug.
2. auth_header() is called on every HTTP request and every WebSocket connection. Per-request HeaderValue::from_str is a non-trivial regex check; pre-validation moves that work out of the hot path.
3. Pre-validation eliminates the need for auth_header to be fallible (its signature is fn auth_header(&self) -> Option<(&str, &str)>, infallible). Per-request validation would require Result<Option<(&str, &str)>, ClientError>, propagating an extra error layer through every call site.
4. Storing as String rather than &str + &str lets auth_header return borrows without ownership tricks; the borrow checker stays simple.
5. The Debug redaction (auth.rs:183-188, 233-238) targets the stored field, so any future contributor adding a Debug derive instead of the manual impl gets immediately surfaced by the existing canary tests (bd:JMAP-sc1b.79 tests bearer_auth_debug_does_not_leak_token and basic_auth_debug_does_not_leak_credentials).

The pre-validate-at-construction pattern is the same one rustls and reqwest's own type designs use; it is not over-engineering.
title: Pre-validated header storage in BearerAuth/BasicAuth (errors at construction, not first request): defend against 'just validate per-request'
